Rainbolt's chem class was an interesting experience. I am giving two stars because the module packets as a physical resource were somewhat helpful to have to study for exams. I took this class with him at 8am Tues/Thurs as there was no other option for 231 that fit my schedule for this semester and I did not want to delay taking this course. Primarily, the time, as someone who is not a morning person, made some of this miserable, but that comes with every early morning class. Rainbolt’s course is set up in a “flipped classroom format” (his words from one lecture), such that he posts pre lecture videos and expects you to watch them prior to attending lecture, even on the first day of classes we were expected to have watched this video as he jumped straight into content and practice. Many of these prelecture videos consisted of examples rather than useful explanations. In class we would typically do problems from his “modules.” The modules are a compilation of written out information on the class topics as well as practice problems. I found this to be a somewhat helpful resource in understanding content, as there was not much explanation in lecture, and the practice problems helped for exam preparation. However, none of the other Orgo professors had this resource, and it cost the students in Rainbolt’s class an extra $35 to get it from the copy center. As for the lectures themselves, they were not at the top tier. He would spend most of the class doing practice problems without really explaining the concepts from them. At the beginning of the semester there would be some explanation, however as time went on there was less and less of this. He would do all of his problems on the chalkboards in the lecture hall, which made it difficult to see beyond the first 5 rows of the lecture hall. He did give us old exams this semester before our exams, but no other resources besides that and the modules. As to his personality I cannot really say much as I had not really interacted with him. To be honest, just do not take an 8am organic chemistry class, but this instructor did not provide us with sufficient materials, which is reflected in the course grades. There is around a 30% curve in this class, with a score in the low 40s being considered as passing. His exams were okay, however there were things on them which we as a class were not sufficiently prepared for. Every week we also had a Canvas quiz which was open on Fridays only. These quizzes were incredibly difficult, and even more so than the exams, with much of the content not being taught in lecture at all. Do with this what you will.

Was not going to take CHEM231 this semester until I saw Dr. Hirschauer teaching it and saw the reviews on planetterp... and they were right. This ended up being the only class out of the four, including two CS courses, that I consistently go. It's a class that Hirschauer makes it fun -- very approachable and understanding, especially from a student perspective.

Dr. Hirschauer is one of the kindest and most understanding professors I've had at UMD. She very obviously cares for her students and wants everyone to succeed, but orgo is still a hard class. She gives you tons of resources, her lectures are very organized, and she always answers questions without making students feel stupid. She also started recording her lectures this semester (Spring 2023), but I don't know if that's a permanent change she's making. She's also a huge pokemon fan and will use pokemon to explain concepts better! The exams are all fair and can be answered with the practice problems or what she goes over in lecture. She doesn't throw any weird curveball questions, but some of them do require a lot of thought. She also gives some extra credit opportunities here and there! Overall, I loved her class. She made me genuinely interested in the content and actually want to come to class. Take Hirschauer yall.

Not exactly sure what these reviews are talking about. This guy is actually the GOAT when it comes to organic chemistry. A lot of people do not like his teaching style with the pre-lecture videos, but those are skippable if you pay attention in lectures and read the modules in class. He can be condescending at times, but if you go to his office hours you can get on his good side. The main point of giving this guy a 5-star rating is that his practice exams PERFECTLY resembled the exams in the class. If a bad rating was given to Rainbolt, it was probably because the student did poorly which they would have done anyways despite the lecturer. Lock in and work harder.

Undisputed orgo I goat professor. Dr.H is actually the kindest and more caring professor I have ever had in the chemistry department at umd. She tries to make everything as clear as possible and will answer any questions asked in her lectures. She gives around 10 homework's and you have 8 tries each so you should get a 100 on all of them. She also gives out 7 quizzes that you take in discussion, but you only have to take 5 of them and your lowest score gets dropped so really its only 4. Regardless, her exams are still difficult, not because she tries to trick you or anything, but because orgo I is just a hard course that requires long hours of studying. She makes it very clear exactly what she expects of us, and provides adequate resources. and extra help to get you going. I think I put in around 20-30 hours per exam, and around 50 hours for the final, and I ended up getting an A in the class. This curve was around 7% or so, which is exactly what she predicted it to be at the very start of the semester. Overall a very good professor, lecturer, and person. Please take her for orgo I if you have the chance!

absolute gem. no other way to put it other than she is a great teacher and really wants her students to succeed and gives so many extra worksheets and problems to work on outside of class. This class isn't easy ofc and you really need to understand the content not just memorize it especially for the tests. the one thing is she does not give practice tests but with the practice sets and all the other stuff ppl are usually fine. just put in the work and go to office hours if you need and you will succeed. also the homework is mad easy so thats a huge plus. there are 5 quizzes in discussion that are 10 mins each and then the other weeks you dont have to go, but I would go because its helpful and basically office hours with you TA.

Dr. Hirschauer is the sweetest professor who really cares about all of her students being successful in organic chemistry. She provides several in-class practice problems and tons of practice problems for outside the class. Organic chemistry itself requires lot of self-studying and practicing, but Dr. Hirschauer does a really good job at explaining the topics in her lectures. Her positive and cheerful attitude was something to always look forward to and she always made organic chemistry a little bit more fun with her Pokemon references every now and then.

Dr Hirschauer is a great lecturer! She is engaging and tries to relate the topics back to things you might now (and includes pokemon references) to make the content more digestible. However, she does drop the ball in some of the later units and especially towards the end her lectures felt very rushed. Her exams are relatively fair but you will not get by simply on memorizing lecture examples and lecture content, you have to KNOW the material, she has many conceptual questions and you will not do well if you do not have a good fundamental understanding of the material. Self studying is a MUST, she says in the beginning you have to put in at least 9 hours of work for this class a week and that is THE TRUTH. She is a good lecturer but she is slightly overhyped and definitely not your ticket to an easy A, you have to WORK for it.

Dr. Hirschauer is fantastic! I loved her teaching style and it wasn't an extremely tiring class (for context, I was in her T/Th 1hour and 15min lecture). I greatly disliked organic chemistry - and I still do even after taking the course - but Dr. Hirschauer made it bearable. She had weekly homework assignments with 8 attempts which helped with keeping up with material. She also had weekly quizzes in discussion sections and she kept the first 5 (not the top 5, but the first 5 you take), though you were still allowed to take more if you wanted more review. Towards the end of the semester, she also decided to drop the lowest of the 5, so only 4 were actually put into the gradebook. The exams were similar to the practice sets she provided, so definitely do those because they are extremely helpful. 
The only complaint I had was that she included a lot of conceptual questions on the exam. In her practice sets, she would include very little - sometimes even none - conceptual questions, and then those sorts of questions would be a great deal of points on the exams. Definitely read over the notes before an exam to really get those conceptual ideas down, because they will 100% be on every exam. Other than that, the practice sets and the exams matched pretty well!!
She made sure to keep things lively during her lecture and her chapter note outlines were very helpful. For class, she completes her lectures based off these outlines she created. Either you download them on your iPad or print them out, because it is difficult to follow her lecture without them. If you are able to bring them to class, then it is very easy to follow!! It keeps your notes very organized and easy to review for exams. 
Overall, she is a kind individual. I would email her sometimes late at night asking questions and she would reply very quickly (I am so sorry Dr. Hirschauer). She wants to make sure you succeed, so take advantage of her office hours and ask her lots of questions. I would definitely recommend her for CHEM231!! 
I am not exactly sure what her policy is for curving, I believe that it is a higher curve when you have a lower grade, but as you are receiving higher grades then the curve is smaller (I think this is it, but I may be wrong). What I do know - from what I have heard - is that the curve for Dr. Hirschauer was the smallest out of the CHEM231 teachers. This is because our class performed well on exams, so if you are looking for a teacher with a biiiiiig curve, Dr. Hirschauer may not be that for you.

Writing for both CHEM131 and CHEM231 here. Dr. Stocker is a great professor – she has many resources for you to succeed and is super helpful during office hours. CHEM231 is a challenging course that requires a lot of work, but Dr. Stocker makes learning the content enjoyable. Exams are fair (and the final is the easiest of them). Overall, I would definitely recommend her.

Fucking love her! She’s entertaining in lecture, wants us to learn concepts rather than random memorization, and just generally cares about us as students. 
It is still a hard class (I maybe spent average of 12-15hr/week and ended with raw B+, but curved to A) but she does things like dropping lowest quiz and homework, keeping highest hw attempt with like 8 attempts, and even gave an extra credit assignment. I really feel like I understand what was happening, and she would also make fun analogies to help explain (she pulled out Pokémon a couple times). 
She started recording lectures a couple weeks in so you didn’t have to go, and discussion was only mandatory first 10 minutes for the quiz (of which you only had to take 5). But it was definitely very useful to actually go, and the people I know who skipped generally did worse.

I must agree that Stocker is the best orgo professor at UMD. She explains things in a very simple way that makes it easy for new students to understand. I believe you will definitely pass for as long as you attend each class, take notes, and do practice problems. Stocker makes the lectures fun and engaging, and she offers a lot of resources/practice problems. I highly recommend reviewing what you've learned each week, as it can go by pretty fast. I had really no problem with Stocker; however, some of the practice exams she gives out do not have an answer key, which was pretty frustrating. I also did not like how there were no notes or recordings posted. I often found myself rushing my notes because she did go pretty fast in lecture and I would be missing some information.
Other than that, her exams were fair (hard) but they did reflect what we learned. Her homework was very hard, and I would highly recommend starting it a week in advance. I also did have a tutor for orgo which helped immensely! I suggest looking into tutoring for this class to help keep up with the information.

I'm someone who doesn't go to office hours, I like to do my studying alone. I heard that her office hours are helpful and has some preference if you really go to them a lot. The midterms are difficult, especially considering the whole curriculum changed this seamster (spring 23) and her practice exams were utterly useless for exams 2 & 3. The practice sets she posts are great and if you use them and go to lecture, listen, review notes you will be fine, she teaches not bad and at a pretty slow pace but a lot of times simplifies things that she later grills you on in the exam that you had no clue about. The saving grace is the final, if you know your concepts you will do great and the curve will get you through. 

Bottom line: not bad professor, teaches at a moderate pace, difficult midterms, really easy final, favoritism for office hour goers. 
Make sure to lock in for this class.

THE MOST AMAZING CHEMISTRY PROFESSOR AT UMD
Not only does she care about her students, but her class set-up and her teaching are so incredible. She provides lesson guides that we fill in which makes it so easy to follow along and actually absorb material without having to worry about writing down everything in time. She had 5 quizzes this semester and dropped one. She has homework almost every week but it didn't take long and you had 8 tries so it was easy to get 100% on all of them.
The midterms were all very very incredibly fair in my opinion. As long as you start reviewing early and start studying at least a week early you're set. You just need to practice practice practice. That's what orgo is, the only way to succeed is practice.
Speaking of practice, SHE PROVIDES SO MUCH!!! This really helped me.
Now I know what you're looking for: CURVE. She does not curve each individual exam, but she curves the median of the class to a C+/B-. I think by the end of the semester is was 4-5% but that just means as a whole the class was doing pretty well so we didn't need more of a curve.
100% take her if you get the chance!!!

She is wonderful and lecturing. If you are taking orgo 1 again please take it with Dixon. After taking it with another professor, Dixon's teaching style if much more simple and understandable. I took this course over the summer, and although you have to go in person everyday, its so worth it. The whole class helped each other and stayed for office hours basically every day. AND yes, she states exactly what kind of questions will be on the exam, no surprises. You will have homework mostly every single day and staying after class for office hours is soooo helpful. 90% of the class will stay in her big office and help each other with the homework. If you have never been to any professors office hours, please let this be the time you actually go because it is not scary or daunting at all!  If you are taking orgo 1 again please dont be discouraged, taking it again with Dixon literally helped sooo much. Taking a summer course with her was a nightmare. The homework was worth 10 points each, and the questions were tough. In addition, if you took the lab the same time as the course you would spend hours doing homework and post lab questions and the lab worksheet. She is helpful during office hours but the class was still extremely hard and painful

I took 231 in Spring '24, and even though it was only my second semester, Dr. H is one of the best professors at UMD, especially for the chemistry department. Her unique teaching style, passion, and dedication made organic chemistry possible and even enjoyable at times. Rather than resorting to boring lecture slides and memorization, she optimized active engagement and stimulated interest during classes, using guided notes, models, and sometimes examples from movies and shows like Star Wars and Pokémon. It was almost like learning from a big kid! 
In addition, Dr. H's exams were fair with material-representative problems with medium difficulty and ample time. No doubt, even though she'll be there to help you every step of the way, you WILL have to exert work and effort to succeed in organic chemistry, so don't expect an easy A. PRACTICE A LOT. There's really no other way to master the material, and Dr. H provides a lot of practice material.
Optimizing studying techniques, going to office hours, and attempting to enjoy the material (it works!) can significantly transform your performance in the class even if it starts bumpy. Try to think of the course as a video game if it helps!
Dr. H genuinely wishes you to do well, so don't hesitate to reach out for questions and tips. She is the epitome of what a professor should be.

Stocker has very engaging lectures and she makes sure to go over what you need to know thoroughly. However, her lectures can be pretty fast-paced at times so it can be hard to note everything down. I had to go over my notes after some lectures because I couldn't spare the brainpower to comprehend anything when I was so busy taking notes. She simplifies things in her lectures to make them easier to understand, then makes the homework and exams really difficult. When I was doing the homework/exam, everything seemed complicated, but seeing the answer key afterward I could totally understand where I made mistakes. Try to not get overwhelmed by the problems since they usually aren't as complicated as they seem. I was a little disappointed that she doesn't post her notes and doesn't record class, so if you miss a class, you can only get second-hand info from a classmate. Make sure to attend class if you want the best shot at succeeding. Discussion is helpful; you go over practice problems and ask the TA questions. You can attend any discussion section and I would recommend going to one every week. The TA I had was very helpful. I would also recommend making a chart or something for all the reactions you have to memorize.

Your grade is based almost purely on the exams (450 points). There are 45 points dedicated to homework. The homework and exams are very tough. For the homework, make sure not to do it last minute because it takes a long time and is graded on accuracy without partial credit for questions. There are 4 homework assignments and the lowest one is dropped. Form or join a study group with your classmates to go over the homework and study for exams. The homework tends to mimic exam questions, so do your best on them. Stocker releases the homework key after it's due but before the exam, so make sure to check your answers afterward. Stocker also posts a lot of practice sets and past exams that you should go over prior to the exams. They are your best study tools. The practice sets and one past exam for each exam have answer keys. When I studied for the exams, I would do every practice set for the content on that exam, then do the one past exam with the answer key. I would then skim the other past exams without answer keys to get a better feel for the types of exam questions there were. The final is cumulative, but was the easiest exam. Don't slack on studying for it though.

Stocker curves, but you don't know what grade you have for sure until the end of the semester. She gives out approximate grade cutoffs after every exam, but they could change depending on how well people in the class do. I ended the class with a low B+ borderline B that got curved to an A.

She provides lecture notes before class. Definitely print them out, or use some sort of electronic device (ex, iPad) to make note-taking easier! LOTS of studying required, pretty good teacher. She explains things a lot better than other orgo teachers, in my opinion.

Dr. H is a really good professor in my opinion and the way she styles her notes is very organized. She mainly teaches from lecture guides that you can print or annotate on your iPad and she's honestly a very funny professor. It's not like she's speaking at you but she like to engage and make sure everyone is learning and understanding what she says. I will say orgo is definitely a hard class but she makes resources very accessible and is lenient on grading so unless you are practicing problems almost everyday up until the midterm using those resources, it will be really hard for you to catch up. The textbook is free but I'd say download the Organic Chemistry Second language book she gives as well as her PP sets, b/c those will really come in handy. AND GO TO OFFICE HOURS!! she's there to help and she won't be rude like some of these other professors you have. if she was teaching 241, i would take her again

I had Dr. Stocker for 131 and 231; she was great for both. She is a good lecturer and explains things clearly and thoroughly without being confusing. She didn't move too fast which was nice and her tests were very fair, always reflecting the material we learned in class. She provided resources for preparing for tests like problem sets and past exams which were very helpful. The only thing I will say about her is she sometimes moves too slow and ends up rushing to teach a lot of material the lecture before the test which can be very frustrating. Orgo is a hard class and taking it with her is no exception but she makes it a lot more palatable.

I actually really enjoyed my class with Rainbolt - the students expressing that he is "rude" or "condescending" have never been told "no" a day in their lives. Seriously. I enjoyed his sense of humor, I liked that he checked students when they acted like they knew more, and that he actually did care. I met with him during office hours several times and told him straight up that I hated chemistry, wasn't trying to get into med school, and just needed to pass. He was a god-send after that and told me that I need to focus on x,y, and z. Which honestly, is super fair. 

I'm a firm believer in the fact that if you approach professors with solutions to your problems, they will help you find the most suitable solution for both of you.

When I took my ORGO I final in the same room as his GEN CHEM II students, his exam mirrored what I took for GEN CHEM II at community college.

She is the goat. She provides a lot of practice problems on ELMS. The GTAs are quite helpful in answering homework problems and general conceptional problems. As people have mentioned, this course is not about memorization. You need to know the "why." I highly recommend completing all of her practice problems to ace this course. She is very passionate in teaching organic chemistry. She provides the time for students to ask questions during lecture. On Halloween, she even dressed up! Again, she is a nice teacher. This course is designed for STEM majors to actually practice good study habits. 

There is a cutoff for the course. So far a C- is about a 50% total grade (this is just from the two midterms and no homework graded). I expect this number to go down after the final. She also provides a handful amount of extra credit too (about 15 points total).
Probably the best professor this year for orgo 1. The lectures were clear, and the exams were easier than the homework.
Great prof take if you can

Dr. Falvey was definitely the best option for orgo 1 this semester. Despite his lecture style being a little unorganized and going off on a lot of irrelevant tangents, he did a good job with explanations and real life applications. A good portion of the grade are weekly homework worksheets (graded on completion) and daily clicker quizzes (annoying bc it means attendance is required, but a good grade booster and allows you to comprehend what you just learned). His exam averages were much higher than all of the other professors (his were about 70-75% whereas other classes were in the 50s or 60s). The exams are very fair and there is 15 extra credit points on every exam. Go to discussion section because I swear you learn more there than in lecture. I would definitely recommend him if he is available.

First, let me say, Dr. Hirschauer is the best professor! She’s funny, engaging, and not passive-aggressive or rude. She’s really knowledgeable and always willing to help you if you’re struggling. Her notes are super organized, and you can either print them out or download them, which makes studying a lot easier.

BUT... that being said, this year, the class was way harder than it was last year. Orgo is hard for everyone, and you have to study A LOT (like weeks in advance), but don't listen to the past reviews if you want an "easy" Orgo class. Dr. H said she "got in trouble" with the chemistry department because her averages were too high, so they made her make the curriculum more difficult?!. As a result, the exams were harder, and the averages were much lower this year. A friend showed me their exam from last semester, and it was COMPLETELY different/way simpler. Most of the questions now are conceptual, and she requires you to memorize A LOT of information. She also doesn't record lectures, which is annoying because sometimes I want to review what she said before an exam, or I feel sick and don't want to attend class. She does post her notes, but honestly, they’re not very helpful because she often explains things without writing them down, leaving very little on the notes. Maybe this will change with time.
 
Don’t get me wrong, I love her so much, but I think everyone in the class had different expectations based on past class experiences and reviews.

He's probably the first professor who's teaching style I really click with. Highly engaging and active. I understand some people might have some critiques of him, but he really makes sure to keep most people afloat with the content. I am kinda sad because I know the class is overall easier than other classes supposedly, but I think that's because he makes the content highly digestible, and I feel like he really tells you what to expect on the exams as opposed to the other professors issues. The extra credit is nice, but it's basically necessary if you want a good grade on the exam. Honestly, he makes organic chemistry such a blast though that I have really been enjoying my time in his class, even at 9 in the morning. I think he's just a really kind guy as well, which of course helps his case a lot.
I would quite literally recommend any other chemistry professor besides Dixon.

Koppel is the GOAT. She is a great lecturer, from what I've heard from others, she goes at a better pace than the other professors. Her exams are decently difficult but they are fair, and as long as you study for them you'll do fine. Although the class averages are fairly low, a 50% is considered passing (at least when it concerns exams). She posts past exams and a whole bunch of other resources on ELMS. Go to lecture because she might provide extra credit for those who show up, but in case you can't her notes are online. Homeworks are easy (only need an 80% for full credit) and she gives plenty of extra credit. Her curve is also very lenient and she will change the curve based on how students do.

I mean wow. Dr. Falvey was an incredible professor. He teaches us things that we would actually see in the real world and his choice of TA and GSS leaders were amazing. His exams are very fair and are mostly based off of the weekly worksheets that we complete. He is such a humorous and kind guy. I think with commitment to the class, as any other class, there is no doubt you will get the grade that you want. I'm not sure if other professors provide extra credit, but Dr. Falvey does! 

I actually really enjoyed taking Organic Chem I and I wish other chemistry professors could be as helpful and considerate as him. You can tell he truly wants you to know how to apply this to real life applications instead of just focusing on abstract and insanely difficult problems that are only seen in textbooks.

Donnie was undoubtedly one of the BEST TA's that I have ever had. He was my TA for Dr. Falvey's CHEM231 course. Donnie is very passionate and truly wants to help you to learn what is going on. I hope that one day he becomes a professor, he would make a great one.

I just loved Dr Falvey. I took him for orgo when I was retaking it and I was terrified of having another rough professor but Dr Falvey made orgo actually enjoyable. He’s funny and he can actually teach so well. He’s very accommodating and you can tell he really cares about our success. I’m really gonna miss him

Best orgo 1 professor you could take, highly recommend taking him as your prof if you have the option. He made a really difficult class super enjoyable and really seemed like he cared about our success. If you take Orgo 1 with him I would not worry too much as long as you put in a ton of effort and do all the work he gives you. W Falvey

Great professor in some ways and in some bad ways. His lectures can be slightly boring, but i will say he is very nice and does try and make orgo fun. His orgo 1 exams consist of his worksheets, so as long as you know how to do his worksheets you're fine, as on the exams they are pretty much a copy and paste on the exam. I think that his TA this semester Donnie was the reason why i did so well in this class. Donnie is really good at teaching and he is good at breaking down problems. Also there were practice exams given to us by Donnie nad if you could do his practice exams you for sure were able to do Falvey's as it was much harder than the actual exam. Also keep your past exams cuz for the final he doesnt post an answer key. The textbook open stax is ok for studying, it does provide some explanation, but i think falvey does do a few more mechanisms that might not be in the book. But again, Donnie's slides are really all that you need to do well in this class. My rec, look at the TA slides with each topic and go to youtube and watch video after video where it shows the mechanisms ( lot of mechanisms to know) and what the product is and write it all out over and over until you can easily recognize the steps, go from small to big. Falvey has grade cut offs not curves, i think it's pretty hard to get a A still as a lot of people were doing really well in his class so a 85 atm is considered an A. Good luck !

One of the best professors you'll get for an organic chemistry course. He is super passionate about what he does, very open to answering questions even after class sessions, and really good at actually getting information through your head. Lectures are great, with clicker questions after each one that accumulates for a sizeable chunk of the final grade. Exams are very congested for a 50-minute timetable.

Dr. Falvey is honestly a joy to have as a professor. His lectures were super engaging and his exams were extremely fair. Donnie is a great TA, the discussion sections really helped me understand the material better. The only downside is sometimes it can be hard to follow Dr. Falvey's writing on the lecture pages, but if you just ask him to clarify he was always willing to help.

There's nothing much to say other than that Dr. Davis is one of the nicest professors at UMD. Although, yes, you probably won't learn much in his class since most of it is going over basic concepts, and he usually expects you to teach yourself the mechanisms. He only grades on 3 midterms and 1 final, all worth 100 points, and the lowest of the 4 are dropped. So if you can manage to do well on the first 3 midterms you don't need to show up for the final. I will say, though, that this class requires you to do a lot of self-studying and a ton, and I mean a ton, of practice problems on your own time. Coming from Dr. Hirschauer in Orgo I, it's a complete shift in teachings. But overall, his exams are manageable, and if you can get above 80%, you're guaranteed an A- at the least. His TA, Nick, is also probably the best TA in the chem department and goes over everything you could possibly need to know about the concepts and mechanisms in his discussions and review sessions.

I have never had a professor this bad until this semester. The only grades are the exams so it’s likely that your grade will be really low unless you’re naturally smart in orgo? Which you probably aren’t. She is also passive aggressive so when reading the older reviews I completely agree with. Her lectures move really fast-moving and she does not post any of her notes, only the slides are posted which don’t give any information on their own. Overall I would suggest moving your schedule around in anyway possible to not take Stocker. In no circumstance would I recommend taking her.

Honestly a solid Chem professor that made CHEM231 a blast for me personally. He has exams that usually test the easier content instead of complex mechanisms, but he also has a lot of freebie points. I really didn't struggle with orgo in the way I was expecting and I studied so overboard that I feel very well prepared for orgo 2 now.  Donnie, the TA, was also a saving grace for the class and made it much more digestible
Very organized course, expectations clearly laid out and exams are fair.

Dr. Falvey is an AMAZING professor for orgo 1. He has weekly worksheets that are couple of pages and worth a completion grade, but doing them fully and understanding everything on them is so important bc his exams are exactly like these ws. For exams, I would just review the worksheets and get A's and B's on the exam. He is a great person, and you will definitely have fun in this class bc of his personality. Def recommend him

A decent professor, she teaches quite quickly. I had her for both Gen Chem 1 and Orgo 1. She does tend to make her midterms quite hard, but the final is easier. Also, she curves the class grades a decent amount.

in my three semesters here i’ve never been prompted to write a review but daniel falvey is so amazing i just have to
orgo is one of the most daunting classes to take but with falvey it was so fun, interesting, and i actually looked forward to his lectures every morning at 9 AM. he is so humorous and engaging! 
clickers are a sizeable portion of the final grade, but they are posted the night before and can be done before class the next day. the worksheets were grade boosters and a big tip to what would be on exams.
there were three midterms which were all extremely fair and rarely had curveballs. it was very concept heavy-falvey encourages learning concepts rather than pure memorization. he does teach in a very different order compared to the other orgo professors, but i (and im sure many others) can agree that his method is better! the final was also extremely generous and reasonable if you paid attention during his classes. 
honestly i never went to discussion after the first week of class but falvey teaches so many examples in lecture i didn’t feel like i missed out on any thing.
donnie was also the most goated TA i’ve ever had.i believe he is the reason i did good. he responds to emails in .00005 seconds and goes above and beyond to make sure you understand everything. 
the downside to this class is that because there were so many tools to do well, the grade cutoff was pretty high for an orgo class and plus/minus are given based on the grades of your peers (like top 6% gets an A+…next 6% gets an A…etc)
all in all, if you are someone who learns based on examples given in class (rather than cookie cutter notes) and are able to self study i’d suggest falvey! if you need a prof to spell things out for you and give you detailed explanations-maybe go with someone else

The absolute sweetest human being. Dr. Falvey was such an understanding, funny, kind-hearted, and patient professor, regardless of whether or not you had the chance to attend office hours or not. Since the very first lecture, he has made clear his passion for the material and his motivation for us as students to have the curiosity for it. Exams were very fair as long as you understood the lecture material and had a decent understanding of the worksheets. Discussions were optional, which was super helpful since I could decide whether or not I needed additional information on material. And for the visual learners out there: he color codes everything. Could not recommend him enough!!!

first off, amazing professor, i couldn't recommend him more. he's a very personable, jolly, charismatic, and encouraging professor, a personality you'd be hard-pressed to find in the chem department. his teaching style is very easy to follow as well, with videos posted after each lecture. there's clickers for every lecture, but he posts the questions in advance. exams are definitely on the easier side compared to the other orgo teachers. he follows the textbook pretty closely and has extra credit questions for each exam that will sometimes ask about concepts covered in the textbook not specifically covered in class. he made orgo a very enjoyable experience, even converting some people to chem majors and encouraging others to take chem courses beyond what was needed for their major. if you're taking orgo 1, there is genuinely not a better prof! just put in the work and you'll have an easy time!!

She's very kind and you can tell she genuinely wants her students to pass and understand organic chemistry, so attending every lecture was not a hard task at all. If you have questions she kindly answers them. However, I feel like the class material (lectures and homework) was too basic and didn't properly capture what you need to get good grades on the exam. The Practice sets she gives are helpful but short and there are no practice tests. Homeworks do absolutely nothing for your grade primarily comes from your exams (which is typical I understand). I heard the previous semester got a lot of extra credit assignments but abused it, I wish she at least gave our semester a chance before eliminating extra credit assignments. Overall, she's an okay choice if you want to take her, but as this is a hard course do not sleep on the multitude of extra resources to supplement your learning (diving the web for additional resources to find extra practice problems because this class has very little is pretty much a silent requirement for this course).

So, this is the unpopular opinion. I think she is the best professor to take for CHEM231 given the pool of professors, but I think that she is a little overhyped. She might have made it harder for my semester specifically because she was red flagged the previous semesters for making her class "too easy", but its irritating to know that you probably worked like an A grade student from previous years, but get a B grade despite others getting As for doing the same level of work you did. She is very good about communication and having an in-person meeting was very accessible. She does care about your success. However, her exams this year were a little weird, like they would follow the practice problem sets that she provides, however some of the conceptual questions would not make any sense or just be hard to figure out. I was told that one of the conceptual questions in one of the exams this semester was answered in the textbook and not the lecture notes. The TA, Praha, was also a little weird, like he was really bad about hiding his annoyance or disappointment when you didn't do something right (sighing loudly or sending passive aggressive emails). In previous semesters, she had quizzes which people said boosted their grades, but she took that away this semester which I thought was annoying. For CHEM231, I would probably take her again if I had the chance because she is probably better than other professors. Also, the practice final exam was very similar to the actual final exam in terms of content, so def focus on that as material (it makes all the content more narrowed down).

Stocker is great, definitely overhated.  Orgo is not easy regardless of the professor.  Took her for 131 and 231.  

Grades- This semester she stopped assigning graded HWs, so the only grades were Midterms (2x100 pts), one quiz (38 pts), and the final (150 pts).  It does put a lot of pressure on the exams but she gives grade estimates after each exam.  Usually A was like 80-100 and B was like 60-80 percent.  If you get over 80% of the total points you're guaranteed an A in the class.  Exam averages usually were around a 60.  Midterms were tough but final was much easier.  Biggest piece of advice is to do every single practice problem (handouts, practice HWs, practice exams).  That was what helped me, didn't need the textbook at all.  

Lectures- I found her lectures easy to follow, she talks slowly and clearly and projects her screen.  Must go to class though because she doesn't record or post detailed notes.  I didn't go to discussion or office hours and was fine.  

Personality- I think she is honestly really funny and tries to make the content engaging (analogies, mnemonics).

There are really a lot of ways this class can go, it's completely up to you. The only grades are exam grades, so the amount of the work you put in is what your grade will reflect. Dr. Stocker's teaching style is very concise, understandable, and engaging. Orgo will never be easy, but I was never confused by the way she taught, which I can't say for most of my classes. She definitely comes off as intimidating at first, but don't let that push you away, and make sure to use your resources. If you are not doing most of the practice exams and homeworks she gives, along with scheduling office hours with Dennis (heavy on this, he's great), you will be in hot water. BUT, if you do those things and take good notes (an iPad is essential since she doesn't post her notes nor records), you'll see that her exams are very fair and reflective of what was taught. Obviously, nobody can teach every little trick in lecture, so you will have to learn those through practice (!!). Her curve is great, but again, every point counts so don't solely rely on that. She can definitely be passive aggressive and visibly has favorites, but if you focus on yourself, your grade will be okay and you will learn the content in the most cohesive way compared to other professors. Like her or not, there's no denying she's a fantastic lecturer and her bob just adds to the experience.

I've never actually left a review for a professor, but I felt I had to because I do actually understand the class content fully, which I don't usually walk away with from a difficult class. Would retake her 100%.

If you are ever choosing to take a lecturer for Orgo 1, choose Koppel! All of her lectures are straightforward and she gives you exactly what you need to know about on exams. She posts her notes online. You don't need to learn any nomenclature past the first exam because she hates it and you only have to memorize about 20 pKas. I know in some other classes, you had to remember IR ranges and other things. She is also more in line with the pace for this class so any late night departmental problem solving sessions will be synced to her class pace. She also has her own late night shows that she records where she'll work out all the problems and stop for questions. Homeworks were a little annoying but you only had to finish 80% of the homework in order to get full credit and the AI tutor that's built in can help you a lot.

Exams are exactly formatted like the ones that she posts online and use the discussions and GSS worksheets for more practice! My discussion TA was really good so he was also able to provide me with more practice problems. Exams were also chunked relatively well. Sometimes she will use questions that are from her old exams verbatim so be sure to look at those! Though the averages were low, the curve was really good!

tl;dr take Koppel for low memorization, good notes posted, helpful late night shows, good curve

HIGHLY recommend taking Hirschauer. The class is incredibly fast paced, but she accomodates for it. She creates lecture notes that you can download or print and fill in the blanks during lecture so you arent worried about writing down everything. She also posts these notes. Exams are hard but doable. I had an excellent grade going into finals and could have got an A, but I focused on my other harder classes since i had a nice "buffer." I got a 50% on the final and still got a B. My advice is to try really hard during the semester on the midterms so the final is easier and doesn't matter as much, because the class will be curved. I had a 10-15 percent curve. Dont put all your trust into that, but if you just stay around or above the average on the exams you'll do great.

I took her for Orgo I and Orgo II lab. Dr. Hirschauer is one of the greatest professors I have ever had. She is so knowledgeable and does such an impressive job of teaching hard concepts to students-- her lectures were so organized and easy to follow (and funny too!). She provides the perfect amount of materials to help students-- fill-in lecture notes and comprehensive practice problem sets. She makes herself very available during office hours, responds to emails quickly, and truly wants every student to understand and succeed. 

As for Orgo II lab, I think she made it far better than the old version of the course. She reduced the amount of work we had to do by getting rid of some post-lab questions and the remaining ones were very clear and problem-based. The overall emphasis was on application and understanding rather than memorization or little details which I really appreciated.

Overall, I'd encourage everyone to take any course that's offered by Hirschauer because she will make the learning process enjoyable and assess you fairly on your understanding.

She is a good lecturer. But this class is difficult because she expects students to have memorized certain things that should not have to be memorized. The concepts themselves are not hard to understand but if you forget one little detail, you will lose points even though you understood the concept behind something. She does not record her lectures or post her annotated slides, which is annoying because to succeed in orgo you have to go over something multiple times. Some of the problems on exams are a bit harder than what she goes over in class but as long as you truly understand the concept behing something (and have memorized certain things), you can still succeed. The entire grade was just 2 midterms, 1 quiz and the final, nothing else. But the curve was great. This class is a test of your ability to memorize very quickly, your attention span and ability to remember lots of info while learning new info. Discussions and GSS were a waste for me personally.

As someone who really was not looking forward to orgo and from reviews of other students saying it's such a hard course, Dr. Hirschauer made it really manageable for her students to pass. I won't lie, her exams were somewhat difficult, considering I heard she had to make it that way due to almost getting in trouble from previous semesters for making it a little easier for her students. Besides that though, she gives a lot of resources for you to really succeed in her class that makes it much more better to pass (PP sets that reflect an idea of what could be on the exam, videos from previous semesters of her explaining topics, etc). Also, her office hours come very in handy; I didn't start going until midway in the semester but the times I went, she would literally come up to you and ask if you had any questions and she would break down topics in order for you to really understand. Also, she has such a fun and infectious energy and you can tell she really likes teaching organic chemistry as well, which made me a little at ease to continue learning orgo, no matter how frustrating it was.

Tips: for midterms, try your best to practice every single day, you don't have to break yourself trying to remember everything in one day but try watching a video and doing some practice problems, whether it be before lecture or after on a topic so you at least understand the concept of each one. Hirschauer really emphasizes explaining how you got to a certain answer rather than just assuming so try your best to memorize mechanisms, products, reaction schemes, etc and try explaining it back to yourself so you can understand much better. working with people also helps so whether you meet people in class or in office hours, don't be afraid to ask them for help and see if you guys want to meet as well.

Disclaimer: i know many people were so worried about whether or not she does a curve but don't depend so much on that. just try to lock in as much in the beginning of the semester that way you won't be too stressed towards the end of the semester. she doesn't usually tell you the curve of the class until the end of the semester but she does give a general overview of the class grades and tips on how to do better on each midterm. I don't know how much the curve was but I do know on the midterms, I scored above or around the average and on the final I got a 69% and ended up with a 71% in the class, but rounded to a B+ as my final overall grade. overall, don't be too hard on yourself, and always reach out to her for help, I promise she does not want you to fail. also shoutout to Aubrey, she was such a great GSS leader for Hirschauer!!

You are my sunshine... my only sunshine....
Falvey, THANK you for being the light of my life this semester. You made organic chemistry, a course that is notoriously hard, much easier to navigate and be successful in than any other professor would. Going into this class, I was nervous (obviously), but I quickly learned that Falvey is such a chill guy who genuinely WANTS you to succeed (unlike other professors in the department). 
The only homework is weekly worksheets that are graded on completion (!!!) and clicker questions that aren't really too hard (as long as you get mostly 3/4 and 4/4 on them, which isn't hard to do, you should be fine because they don't take up a huge chunk of the grade).
The reason why I didn't end up hating CHEM231 is because of how fair the exams were. Like seriously. No curveballs. Literally just do the homeworks, go to lecture, study for exams at least a week in advance if you have to, and you should be getting A's and B's on the exams. Just do the work. Our TA this semester (shoutout to Donnie!!) was so chill and I personally thought he was good at answering any questions I had. I didn't have the time to go to office hours but I also heard that Falvey's office hours were really helpful too (apparently he is so good at explaining stuff that students taking other professors would go to his office hours). The average was usually in the 70s (which is really good for orgo, trust me), and the a/b cutoff was an 85 at the end. Also, before each exam, he would literally say outright that the questions from each exam would be ***directly taken*** from the weekly worksheets and clicker questions (they wouldn't be exactly the same question, but you would attack the question the exact same way)... so if you show up to class and do the worksheets, you'll be fine. I was an idiot and never really tried on those so I had to study more for the exams, but I PROMISE if you consistently show up to class and do fine you'll be bing chilling
TLDR if you have the chance, take falvey, not anyone else. Trust me. Your future self will thank me. I just wish he was teaching orgo 2 next semester, but oh well. Wish me luck

Highly recommend. Her door is almost always open to ask for help. Anytime I emailed her about a question, she usually got back in a day or less. You have a lot of resources to work with. Her PP sets come with video explanations that are a godsend. For lecture, she creates outlines so you can just download the PDF onto your iPad and follow along. It's really convenient since you can spend more time trying to understand what she's saying. She doesn't record her lectures but released some of her old video lectures from quarantine on certain chapters. Discussion is pretty much pointless except for the practice quizzes. GSS was helpful when reviewing for exams. They gave us some test-taking tips and had some pretty hard but clever problems on their worksheets. I don't think I touched the online textbook past week 2. If I didn't know something, I'd just google it or email her. 

For classwork, the only thing that's graded is homework (about 10 canvas quizzes), 3 midterms and a final. Homework is purely a grade boost since you have 8 tries. You can straight up ask her for help 
on it and she'll explain it to you. Make sure you understand the concepts on the homework and aren't just clicking random choices until you get a 100. I did that a couple times and then the same concept showed up on the exam. For midterms, the first midterm caught me by surprise due to how fast-paced the exam was. After that, I came in a lot more prepared and was able to pace myself through the exam. Some of the conceptual questions are tricky, especially when they ask you to rank compounds by a certain criteria. Everything else is pretty straightforward and comes straight out of lecture. 

Tips: Treat the PP sets as absolutely necessary and do them well in advance before the exam. This gives you time to ask questions if the video explanations don't cut it for you. Also, the department problem solving sessions are very helpful. It was done by the entire department so you'll get to see how other professors tackle a topic. Sometimes, you'll hear something explained differently and it'll just click really well.  Overall, make use of the resources given to you.

She does not record lectures. Homework is not timed and you get 8 tries. They are automatic points. She curves the class so that the B/C cut-off is where the class median was. Our class median was around 60%, so I got an A- with a 79%. Her exams are a little bit of a curve ball, but I heard that this semester's exams were more difficult.  The TA, Praha, has been working with her for a few semesters now but he is terrible. Discussion is a waste of time, and he is extremely rude. He got an attitude when people stopped showing up and refused to release discussion keys on canvas.

With no exaggeration, this was the easiest course I had taken this past semester. Do not get me wrong, as with organic chemistry, the material is difficult. Expect yourself to spend a lot of time outside of this class reading, memorizing, and practicing content. That being said, Falvey is a great professor. He is fun and pretty nice, as well as very eager to answer questions (go to office hours). I never got bored in his class, mainly because he made orgo interesting and wrote the notes and problems as the lecture progressed as opposed to showing slides. He engages in the class well, and quite literally remembered more than half the classes' names by the end of the semester. I was also lucky with the TA, whose discussions acted as supplemental lectures where you solidify the learning you get from Falvey's. The exams: extremely fair. If you just do practice problems, review the homework's, and read the book/reread the slides you'll get a B guaranteed. For an A, I would say just going over and over the mechanisms and reactions (i.e. repeatedly writing them down on a white board from memory) got me an A+. Plus, extra credit.

Koppel is a sweet and well-spoken instructor. She provides all the tools necessary to succeed and makes herself available for any questions or comments. One thing to look out for is her exams. They're tough. However, her grading curve is insane. Your best bet will be her past exams. Her TA discussions aren't as helpful, but they allow you to ask a TA about a practice problem or concept. Her homework and quiz grade helps boost your grade at the last minute. She also provides a plethora of extra credit opportunities throughout the semester. If you're willing to work hard and connect with her, you'll get a good grade in her course.

This man is so overrated. He's cute and all cause he's just an adorable old guy (major Santa Claus energy)...HOWEVER he did NOT prepare us well for Orgo 2 at all. If you're stopping at Orgo 1, then take him. But if you're planning on taking Orgo 2, then HELL NO please take anyone else !!!!

Dr. Stocker was the best professor I've ever had at UMD! She was very organized and good at thoroughly explaining difficult concepts. She is very conceptual, and expects you to understand the material, not just memorize it. It's very important to go to lecture and office hours. DO THE PROBLEM SETS. DO THE PRACTICE EXAMS. Her exams can be difficult, but if you thoroughly review the practice exams and problem sets, go to office hours, go to gss, etc. you will do really well on the exams. Also, her final was very fair.

Excellent Professor. Great example of hard subjects can be broken down easily. He presents content in a straightforward way, interacts with the class often, and posts lots of resources for different learning styles. Over a dozen students got 100 on exams every time. I got an A in my lab and am understanding Orgo 2 easily due to the foundation he set me up on. His exam questions were always the same format as his homeworks.

There are a lot of bad reviews, these people are probably very salty in my opinion. Dr. Dixon goes above and beyond to personally help students and wants everyone to succeed in her class. She offers extra credit opportunities before every exam, and she always scores her exams such that you can skip an entire question and still get 100%. I'm doing bad in this class because I'm frankly very lazy personally, but there is EVERY opportunity to make sure you get an A in this class. You just have to take it. Here are some tips for future students:
1. Keep up with the content. If you fall behind, it can be stressful to catch up (although not impossible). I personally was always behind, but once I caught up, I realized that if I had just reviewed or learned a little bit everyday, things would've been so much easier. 
2. briefly review the content you will learn in lecture BEEFORE attending lecture. Even if it's just watching a youtube video without understanding what's going on, familiarizing yourself with the content will make understanding what's being taught during lecture much much easier. First time seeing the content -> familiarize. second time (lecture) -> learn. after lecture, review the notes, attempt the beginner sets provided, and watch other youtube videos if you need another perspective on the content. Ask TAs or got to office hours to clear up any complicated/confusing problems you encounter, or concepts. Do this for every chapter, before it's time for the next one.
3. Make sure you understand everything in the notes if you can. Even if it is a small detail, make sure you don't forget it, because on the exams there were often trickier problems that included those little details or exceptions, which is a main thing that contributed to exam difficulty. But obviously prioritize the "big picture" concepts first if you are on a time crunch.
4. DONT underestimate the amount of time you need to dedicate preparing for the exams. I spent several hours the week before exam week doing practice problems and reviewing/learning, but on the exam the questions always had these little things I was unsure about, and I would get points off here and there that added up to a LOT of points taken off. So start reviewing chapters you just learned as soon as possible, and I mean the day of or after you just went over it in lecture. This way you have time to get to really know the content, which is absolutely necessary for doing well. 
5. do every practice problem provided and if you got something wrong, make a physical note of what you did wrong and why. If you dont know why, go back to the notes bcs the answer will be there 90% of the time. I really wish I did this from the start...
6. try to understand the reasoning behind every answer, dont just try to memorize patterns (unless specifically stated in lecture to memorize) because sometimes it depends on certain conditions and situations. This one is kinda hard to explain, but you might get what I mean after starting the semester.
7. Be sure you are able to complete problems quickly (but also dont rush, leading to careless mistakes). Exams had 15 problems with 1 hr 15 mins to complete...however, most of the problems took several minutes, esp the ones where you have to draw products or mechanisms. Basically, know the content well enough so that you are able to get through problems fast. Try timing yourself when doing practice problems, and if you notice the time is too long then think of ways/methods you can become more efficient.
8. test taking tip: during the exam, spend more time on problems you know you can get an answer to. If there is a concept you weren't able to study for and feel very unsure about, just put your best answer and dont spend too much time on it, because you will run out of/ waste a lot of time when you couldve used that time to complete other problems you are more likely to get right. the time goes by FAST and even when I studied a lot, I had to work really quickly just to complete all the problems before time was up. 
9.  If you are struggling to even start learning content, go to GSS because those problems are often simpler and can help you adjust. 
I was really impressed with the TAs Aubrey and Alice because they break things down in a way that even a little kid could understand.

Overall, I would definitely recommend Dr. Hirschauer for Orgo 1. Just make sure to hit the ground running and try not to fall behind. For context I am an average student who procrastinates a lot but often manages to do well enough to get A's (might get a B in this class though, I just didn't take it as seriously as I should've).
